locator.section: Table 2 Model 5, all coefficient rows, random effects, log likelihood and AIC

finding: For log likelihood -41141.37 and AIC 82338.74, rounding intervals imply k in [27.9925,28.0075], compatible with 28. There are 28 printed fixed coefficients alone; random variances and a linear-model residual variance require additional parameters under ordinary marginal ML AIC. Hence the pair is difficult to reconcile with the described full mixed model. ML/REML choice and AIC convention are undocumented, so this remains a conditional diagnostic, not a claimed correction.

finding: The Model 2 fertility cell is blank, unlike Models 1 and 3 and MAIN’s general controls description. Log likelihood -140933.12 and AIC 281932.2 imply k in [32.95,33.01], allowing 33. locator.section: Table A1, Women’s part-time employment S.D., range and Mean N

finding: The part-time S.D. is printed 0.23 while the range is 5.09–60.58 for N=143 survey-level observations. Even taking the closest endpoints allowed by rounding (5.095 and 60.575), any unweighted distribution containing those endpoints has population SD at least 55.480/sqrt(2×143), over 3.28; a sample SD is no smaller. This cannot be the printed SD on the same percentage scale. A different weighting/scale is not documented; do not substitute an inferred SD.

MAIN describes GDP per capita, whereas the supplement labels GDP index. The source dictionary distinguishes a logged/bounded index from raw PPP GDP per capita. They are not merely unit conversions; both readings are retained as uncertain, without choosing from observed values.

Methods call business size the log of full-time employees plus one; limitations explicitly state that full-time versus part-time status is unknown. The available OMNOWJOB dictionary supplies headcount, not FTE/full-time employees. The origin therefore labels headcount and flags that choice rather than fabricating hours.

MAIN says in the labor force but its footnote and S1 contrast the primary sample with people who are not employed. Labor force includes unemployed job seekers, so employment-only and labor-force inclusion are not the same rule. The packet does not settle the coding.

MAIN defines an established owner through current ownership/management without the source’s more-than-42-month cutoff. It quotes a start-up screen but also adds an active/payment-duration nascent definition. Harmonized OMESTBBT and SUBOANWT cannot be assumed to be the exact author variables; no empirical count matching is used to resolve this.

Methods explicitly define more than five additional employees; results say hire more than five employees. The closest implementation uses future minus current count, while total future count is recorded as non-equivalent. No coding script is present to settle the looser wording.

The prose reductions use squared printed SDs, not SD differences. The printed female coefficient –.57 permits exp(b) rounding to 0.57. The prose reciprocal 1/0.57=1.75 and broad about-1.8 description are compatible with rounding uncertainty of the underlying coefficient/odds ratio. These quantities are odds ratios, not female/male probability ratios.

check: Boundary random effects and missing test details
finding: Several SDs print zero or near zero. For example .0000 denotes a nonnegative SD interval up to roughly .00005, not an exact zero established by printing alone. Boundary-aware LR inference, convergence, covariance correlations, Hessian diagnostics, test df and full empty-model output are absent. Their adequacy cannot be adjudicated from the table.

Both notes say SEs are in parentheses, but these tables display separate Coef./S.E. columns without parentheses. Table 2 actually uses parentheses. PDF layout was checked so the separate columns were transcribed correctly.

Expanding the printed inclusive year ranges and listed individual years gives 143 country-year entries, agreeing with the stated survey count. This checks document structure only and does not establish source availability or individual sample sizes.

The roster includes France 2003 while the supplied dictionary says its work and education items lack substantive responses. Status responses are absent in 2001–2002 in both listed GEM sources even though those years enter status-controlled models. These are source/version or undocumented-processing gaps, not evidence from raw data and not established MAIN/S1 numerical contradictions.

Each printed two-decimal year share represents a rounding interval of width .01. In each panel, the sum of all eight intervals contains 1, so displayed shares need not sum exactly to 1 and do not establish an inconsistency.

The business-size model is on a log(count+1) scale despite a table header referring to employees and a plot axis labeled Business Size. No inverse-log or smearing correction is reported; exact headcount predictions must not be inferred from these displayed values. Other figures show fixed-part conditional probabilities, not random-effects-integrated population means.
